## Bonus B1 — Working with tabular data (Reference)

n8n is built for tables. Every node passes a list of **items**, and one item = one row. The whole exercise is about that idea.

```
Table (array) → Split Into Rows → Add Revenue Column → Keep Strong Sellers → Sort By Revenue → Collect Rows → Write Readout (LLM)
                (one item per row)   (computed column)    (Filter)              (Sort)            (Aggregate)    (narrate, don't calculate)
```

**The lesson:** do the *maths* with nodes and expressions (revenue, totals, filtering, sorting) — they are exact and repeatable. Use the LLM only to *narrate* the result. An LLM asked to add up a column will sometimes get it wrong; a Set node never does.

## The four tabular primitives

- **Split Out** — turns one item holding an array into many items, one per element. After this node, click it and read the panel: 10 rows.
- **Set (Add Revenue Column)** — adds a *computed column*. `={{ $json.price * $json.units_sold }}`. Runs once per row.
- **Filter** — drops rows that fail a condition. Same condition editor as the IF node, but no branches: rows either pass or vanish.
- **Sort** — orders the rows by a field.
- **Aggregate** — the opposite of Split Out: collapses many rows back into one item with an array field (`top_dishes`), so the LLM can see them all at once.
